title: What is known about 1RB0LB_1RC1LD_1LD0RD_1LE0RC_1LF---_0LA1RF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LB_1RC1LD_1LD0RD_1LE0RC_1LF---_0LA1RF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The transition table is the mirror image of the holdout 1RB0LB_1RC0LA_1RD---_0RE1LD_1LF0RF_1LA1RB's with the states renamed (A,B,C,D,E,F of that machine are C,D,E,F,A,B here), so the run is that machine's dynamics started in its state E. It shows the same glider system, mirrored: a gun at the right end, a slowly growing structure at the left end.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 31,456 cells have been visited and 23,567 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Same table as 1RB0LB_1RC0LA_1RD---_0RE1LD_1LF0RF_1LA1RB, mirrored
claims.text: Mirror the moves of 1RB0LB_1RC0LA_1RD---_0RE1LD_1LF0RF_1LA1RB and rename its states A→C, B→D, C→E, D→F, E→A, F→B: the result is this table. Only the start state differs (this machine starts where the other would be in E).

claims.title: The two sweeps over the background
claims.text: Going left, B crosses (1^8 00)^n in 30n steps and leaves ((011)^3 0)^n; going right, D crosses ((011)^3 0)^n in 38n steps and leaves (1^4 00 1^4)^n.

claims.title: The left end grows in rare events
claims.text: Up to 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps the left end grows in 33 bursts (at steps 5230, 11061, 24512, …, 854869638, 1183687075, 1640256864).

claims.title: Gliders, merges and a counter
claims.text: The defect picture is the mirror image of the other machine's: gliders are born at the right end, travel left, merge and pile up near the left end.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.113). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.552).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Next step: Analyse 1RB0LB_1RC0LA_1RD---_0RE1LD_1LF0RF_1LA1RB first; the glider catalogue and its rules carry over by the mirror symmetry.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine is the mirror image of another holdout, 1RB0LB_1RC0LA_1RD---_0RE1LD_1LF0RF_1LA1RB, started in a different state: its tape is a repeated word with defects that move like particles between a glider gun at the right end and a slowly growing pile at the left end.

facts.text: Same table as 1RB0LB_1RC0LA_1RD---_0RE1LD_1LF0RF_1LA1RB, mirrored and renamed.
Bursts of growth at the left end in 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps.
No halt in the C simulator; 31,456 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: The same machine, seen in a mirror
html: Swap left and right in the table of 1RB0LB_1RC0LA_1RD---_0RE1LD_1LF0RF_1LA1RB and rename its states A,B,C,D,E,F as C,D,E,F,A,B: you get exactly this table. The only difference is where the run starts: this machine starts in the state that the other calls E. So everything about the background and the gliders carries over, mirrored; the particular sequence of gliders does not.

sections.heading: Gliders from right to left
html: As in the mirrored machine, the head shuttles out from the right end and turns back at a defect or passes it depending on the defect's shape, so the defects act as the digits of a counter. The right end (the fast-growing side) is a glider gun; the gliders drift left, merge, and accumulate near the left end, which grows by a few cells in rare bursts (33 in 3·109 steps). A halt (E reading 1) needs a defect of the right shape where the head turns.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.113). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.552).
After 109 steps the tape spans 31,456 cells (125 left of the start, 24,470 right), with a density of 1s of 0.749.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: The table of 1RB0LB_1RC0LA_1RD---_0RE1LD_1LF0RF_1LA1RB mirrored and renamed, started in that machine's state E: the same bouncer over 1^8 00 / (011)^3 0 with gliders from the gun at the right end to a slowly growing left end.
